captions.text: After an interruption, two similar screws can become
a guessing game.
PartCue keeps their pickup and origin visible beside
the work. This is the actual Lens Studio
preview. The bench is simulated, with four
authored parts and predefined origins.
Select each part and its tray well, then
record the removal.
Every mark is an explicit choice, so the
return follows your own recorded sequence.
Now the last recorded part becomes the first return.
Amber marks the pickup, cyan marks its
origin. A wrong choice cannot advance the record.
The correct selection and confirmation move forward once.
Pause clears the work cues.
Resume restores the same next part.
Undo brings back the previous return, so a
correction does not lose context.
Confirm the remaining parts, and the path disappears
when all four returns are accounted for.
These are user confirmations.
The Lens does not verify physical installation.
Restart asks for confirmation before clearing the session.
The Lens keeps its own session.
The separate companion handles saved job records.
Here is the web companion, running in the
browser. You can rehearse the same workflow and
keep a record between visits.
It does not synchronize automatically with the Lens.
The two experiences have separate sessions.
The companion provides a place to review and save
those job records.
Start as a guest, or sign in to
save a job.
Record a few parts, then save the session
to your account.
After reloading the page, load that saved job
and carry on from the same point.
Accounts keep saved jobs separate.
Guest work needs explicit saving or export.
Export creates a portable record.
Import checks the file before opening it as a
new session. A broken file leaves your current
work untouched. Saved revisions stop an older browser
tab from silently overwriting a newer job.
Portable files also support deliberate backups and handoffs.
The goal is less reconstruction after an interruption.
That still needs testing with repairers, including the
time spent recording.
Glasses comfort and physical alignment also need device
testing. Mats, photographs and a plain reverse
checklist are the baselines to beat.
This demonstration shows the software behavior.
PartCue was created by Shivam Gupta with AI
assistance. It helps you follow your own record,
one part at a time.
Every part has a way home.
